title: D-Tracker: Modeling Interest Diffusion in Social Activity Tensor Data Streams

problem.claim: The task is to discover temporal patterns in social activity data and accurately forecast future activities.

gap.claim: Existing modeling and forecasting of social activity data streams is difficult because the data are high-dimensional and contain multiple time-varying dynamics, including trends, seasonality, and interest diffusion.

contributions.claim: D-Tracker continuously captures time-varying temporal patterns in social activity tensor data streams and forecasts future activities.

D-Tracker incorporates a partial differential equation into a tensor decomposition framework to model trends, seasonality, and interest diffusion between locations interpretably, without hyperparameters, and with computation time independent of time-series length.
The authors provide source code and datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on GoogleTrends web search volume data and COVID-19 infection data reportedly show higher forecasting accuracy in less computation time than existing methods.
The experiments reportedly extract interest diffusion between locations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Social activity data reflect people's interests and activities, motivating temporal analysis and forecasting.
The data are difficult to model and forecast because they are high-dimensional and combine several time-varying dynamics.
The paper proposes D-Tracker to continuously capture time-varying patterns and forecast future activities.
D-Tracker is described as interpretable, automatic, and scalable.
Experiments on web search and COVID-19 data report improved forecasting accuracy, lower computation time, and extraction of interest diffusion.

source_observation.claim: The method models multiple time-varying dynamics, including trends, seasonality, and diffusion between locations, within a tensor decomposition framework.

interpretation.claim: A structured model can represent several interacting temporal phenomena while retaining an interpretable decomposition.

application.claim: For high-dimensional streaming data with heterogeneous temporal behavior, consider combining domain-informed dynamics with tensor decomposition.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported social activity datasets or dynamics.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets' sizes, time spans, or preprocessing.
The abstract does not identify the compared existing methods or quantify accuracy and computation-time differences.
The abstract does not describe the partial differential equation, tensor decomposition, or forecasting procedure in detail.
The abstract does not report limitations, statistical uncertainty, or evaluation protocols.
